data.text: I travel to Saigon often for business and like staying in this area of District 1. It's close to a nice park and lots of restaurants, and the streets lined with towering trees is delightful. I have stayed at Little Brick several times over the last year. But this time will be the last. It no longer deserves its 8+ rating on Booking. com and elsewhere. Staff sleep in the lobby and were not polite. They now charge for water when almost every hotel gives a couple of bottles free. Rooms are still clean but getting tired. Wallpaper peeling from the walls, lightbulbs that don't work or don't fit into the lamp so they give off bad light. With so many hotels in district 1, you can do better. Go somewhere else.

It was also the local waterhole for the many scribes sent to cover that conflict and it is without any doubt that they soaked up cocktails like dry sponges. Just as we did, in their honour. I can highly recommend the Saigon Special, a delectable spiced number enhanced with slices red chilli. Warm, fuzzy and sublime. Go easy on the salted nuts as these will heighten your thirst and you’ll need assistance to your room or taxi. The staff are very attentive, polite and friendly.

The baths have a full-size spa bath, and a glassed-in space with a shower and toilet. The hotel reception staff are friendly and helpful. It's in an extremely convenient location for visiting the old town, or the night market, and about 30-45 minutes bike ride to the beach. It is possible to spend too much time in Hoi An -- if you're spending more than 3 nights, make sure you book a day trip elsewhere (I enjoyed the Marble Mountains in Da Nang). We booked a car to the airport for 14 usd using a travel agency in the old town. I wished I stayed longer and relax in this town and hotel.

data.text: My family and I stayed for 3 nights at Ninh Binh Panorama Homestay. The location, accommodation, food & hospitality by the hosts exceeded expectations. The bungalow was fully equipped with comfortable beds, fans & a great shower. The porch had a hammock & full oudoor setting with tea & coffee facilities. The food was always fresh and delicious. I recommend the mango smoothie and spring rolls! The homestay has free bicycles to use and it was a great way to see the surrounding area. We also hired scooters which are available onsite. We weren't in a rush to explore because it's easy to lose track of time enjoying the scenery surrounding the homestay. I highly recommend this homestay. It really felt like a home away from home in an incredibly beautiful part of Vietnam.

Would not stay again and would not recommend it for anyone else.

Our room was very tired and faced the road. The road noise was loud. I notice that neighbouring hotels have just not built rooms that face this direction - a wise choice. The beach was not raked or cleaned is any way, the litter was horrid. Again, it should be noted that other hotels in the area seem to clean their portion of the beach regularly. Having stayed at various hotels and resorts on PQ, this one just doesn't seem worth the money.

On the plus side, our room was fully air-conditioned and had a mini bar, the staff were very friendly, plus sun loungers and towels are available at the pool area, which overlooks the river. data.text: Booked this hotel based on good reviews. Stayed 4 nights. First we got a room with a window that faced a interior wall. We asked to change and then got a room that had a window with some natural light but it smelled sooo strong of mildew! My clothes all picked up the odour. We put up with it rather than move again. We had such an amazing experience in Hanoi with such amazing staff that we were expecting similar. It was not the case at this hotel. Staff at reception didn’t even look up from their phones when you were in the lobby. The pool area was nice and breakfast was satisfactory, other than that I would say go elsewhere. We moved to another hotel in Hoi An for the remaining 4 days and it was amazing!!

data.text: Great option for backpackers wanting to stay in their low daily budget, nice clean rooms, amazing staff and nice atmosphere in the centre of Nha Trang, one of the most unfriendly and spoiled by tourism places in Vietnam. The only bad thing is that the aircon in our room was noisy and hardly cooled the room down. Wifi was ok. A great thing about this place is that if you leave Nha Trang in the evening you can safely leave your luggage there for the day and collect it in the evening before your bus, also you can take a shower which is available for free on the ground floor by the lobby and you can get a towel if you don't have your own for 5k dong to dry yourself after that. We wanted to take overnight train so this advantage convinced us to stay there. Would recommend !

data.text: The Saigon Prince hotel was great, found the moment our group arrived from a long flight, we were greeted from the friendly hotel staff. The room are clean, spacious but nothing flash or grand. Personally found everything very comfortable. The gym was tiny, appeared much more spacious on their website, however they had enough equipment to get a good workout. They had plenty of dumbbell weights just outside the main gym. No access to the steam room & sauna unless you paid extra. Felt that was average as most hotels include these facilities under a hotel guests lodging fees. Location is perfect, plenty of open area outside to walk, run & exercise which my group of 12 did. Shopping nearby, good restaurant too. Highly recommend a stay at this hotel.

data.text: I have been privileged to travel in many countries over the last 46 years. I have been to several resorts whether they be in the Caribbeans, Hawaii, Mainland US or Europe. Never have I been so surrounded with luxury, a beautiful site but most importantly a staff that really demonstrated care, desire to serve their clients well and done so always with a smile. When I was checked in I was fully informed of the complimentary options such as breakfast (from 630a-930a on the 9th floor), the coffee & tea, and the costs of the minibar options. Hana and I talked about what I had already done in Da Nang and Hoi An and then proceeded to tell me about the other activities and sites that the surrounding area has to offer. data.text: This is the 4th time we've stayed at Green Village and we'll continue to come back. This little oasis is our most favourite place to stay in VN - it's just so relaxing. Excellent food, fantastic bamboo huts complete with big comfy beds with mozzie nets, huge lovely bathrooms, bar fridge and fans, perfect balcony. And now a new pool! As we've been here often we don't bother with tours any more, but take advantage of the free bikes and the many paths along the canals. But the best thing about Green Village? The people. data.text: We stayed for 4 nights in order to see Saigon, go on the Mekong and visit the Cu Chi Tunnels. The hotel is right by the Saigon River and close to the Opera House. The rooms, food (especially the selection of food for breakfast) and service were all very good. All staff were most helpful. There is a busy road outside with hundreds of scooters on it but it did not impact on our stay. We found it interesting watching the traffic. One man went by with a new fridge on the back of his scooter and it was common to see families of 4 on a scooter. The traffic does not stop when you are on a crossing it just goes around you!

data.text: We feel lucky to have spent 3 nights at Murrays GH. Definitely appreciated the cleanliness, layout and staff, and of course we took advantage of Wayne's time to learn more about Vietnam culture and customs. The assistance booking our tickets for the boat to PP was great. Moreover, the city really does merit more than just a "fly by" one nighter before border crossing. Take advantage of the bikes on offer at the GH and follow the route they will lay out for you - it's flat and a lovely look at the countryside, and folks along the way are very friendly! We also walked to the market along the riverfront. My advice is spend 2 or 3 nights and explore the city and surrounds further!

data.text: Back again after 2 years. Room rates are reasonable and all rooms have balcony with magnificent view of the river. Early morning starting from 5. 30 am one can see intrepid swimmers frolicking in the Mekong River. They will swim till 7. 30 am . Hence don't forget to wake up early to see this unique sight of My Tho. Do order Hu Tiu My Tho for breakfast. Hu Tiu My Tho is a Rice Noodle specialty of this town consisting of shrimps, pork, liver, squid and ribs. The hotel is also an embarkation point for boat cruise to the nearby island of Con Phung and Con Thoi Son. Both have fruit orchards and one can take photos with Python or feed the caged crocodiles with lumps of decaying meat. A trip worthwhile. Once again relatively this is the boondocks and hotel rooms standard cannot aspired…

The service was consistently excellent - from front desk to pool attendants. This is probably the only hotel in Saigon that I would book, and if I ever come back, it will be the first reservation I make.

data.text: I stayed at Four oceans (also called Bon Bien) with my two kids and we really enjoyed it. The receptionists are very nice and welcoming, the grounds are beautiful and very well kept. The pool is fantastic, and the hotel has direct access to the beach with it's own lounge chairs. This part of the beach is great as Mui Ne has a serious sand erosion problems at some parts further up, so choose your hotel wisely! Breakfast was really nice with views of the beach. The rooms are aging and could use some upgrading but it did not bother us. The only negative was that on our last night some guests were having Kareoke and it was loud until past 10 pm, I hope management will not allow this in the future as it is disrespectful to other people. I would stay again and recommend this hotel.

A real plus is that The Scarlett is tucked away in a quiet alley, so is quiet, but is walking distance to the main ( part pedestrianised) restaurant /bar area; and the river. Comfortable room ( though not that big). Staff very efficient and helpful with advice and arrangements for excursions.

data.text: I stayed here in September on 2 occasions. I found the hotel to be placed in a good position for view from room, for proximity to good restaurants, cafes, street food stalls as well as tourist sites. There a number of great little cafes at the large roundabout on Tran Cao Van St, just a short walk around the corner. It's certainly got novelty factor: from the grand decadent (and now slightly dirty and rough round the edges) dining room to reception. From my feeling, the service was quite good for a 5-star Vietnam hotel, the staff was nice, and the breakfast was delicious. But the things which caught my impression the most were the small stuff in my room: some tags in the wardrobe, on the table next to the bed, on the hanger, brush, comb, and even the shave. They all were to protect the environment or encourage people to save our planet. That was amazing cus I haven’t seen any hotel like that before. And those little things really made my day. Love this hotel and I will come back next time.

data.text: We arrived at Little Hoi An Beach Hotel after a hectic week of work in Can Tho. This was an excellent place to unwind and begin our vacation. The suite could handle minor renovations and the decor is slightly dated There were a few spots on the walls, not all power outlets worked, and the South facing windows didn't move smoothly (brand new windows on the opposite side worked flawlessly). But the size of the suite did wonders…

We also hired mopeds for $5 a day, or you can borrow bicycles for free. It's about a 15-minute cycle or 5-minute drive to Hoi An centre, and about a 10-minute drive to An Bang beach. The villa itself is gorgeous - right by the river, quiet, clean, and with a wonderful swimming pool and terrace. Breakfast choice was varied and tasty. We were lucky that it wasn't very busy when we were there (it only opened Feb 2018), but I would mainly recommend this for families,…

data.text: We stayed in the double bungalows which were lovely, the ceiling fan did a great job of keeping us cool in the hot summer and the bed was really comfy. The garden setting is beautiful and the hosts cooked us incredible food - lots of it! We booked a package, 2 nights accomodation and tours which was gave insight into Mekong Delta life, from visiting local workshops, cooking sweets with a local lady, exploring the island on bike and by boat. Our guide, Mr Nhan was very knowledgable and wonderful at answering our many questions with a smile. It was very relaxed and certainly rustic - you can hear roosters crowing and other farm animals but we enjoyed hearing all the local sounds. I would recommend a Mekong Rustic tour to anyone wishing for an authentic experience.

Wouldn't fault the staff nor the amenities you get here but if all rooms smelt like that I would be put off staying again.

That said: we only had one full day in Hanoi, which is to say that were were barely at the hotel. There are several other not-as-nice but not-as-expensive hotels in the area and in hindsight, those probably would have been a better choice for us on this trip. However, for the cost in USD compared to hotels in the US - definitely a great value. But as far as how far you can stretch your money in Hanoi, possibly something to consider.

Elsewise, use Google Translator. They have strong wifi there. It is within walking distance to the bus stop, market and food area. data.text: We stayed for two nights in this hotel either side of our trip to Halong bay. Despite being situated in the hectic and noisy Old Quarter, the rooms we stayed in (we were upgraded on both instances) were quiet. In addition to large beds, a delicious breakfast, and excellent bathrooms the staff were quite exceptional. All spoke excellent English, were consistently helpful and polite and very friendly. The hotel stored suitcases for us whilst we were away at Halong Bay and a member of staff even carried a bag for us to the tour operator. The staff booked cars to collect and drop us off at the airport, if you're staying in Hanoi, look no further.

data.text: We spent New Year 18/19 at Six Senses, having had an amazing two weeks in Vietnam. We thought it would be great to wind down before returning home, however, despite many promises, there was literally nothing to do. All snorkelling / water sports were cancelled whilst we were there, which was the key point for our teenagers. Six Senses is expensive before you go, but as a captive audience it is unbelievably expensive when you get there. For a 1 litre bottle of pineapple juice we were charged $25. Tough when your family only drink water / fresh juice rather than fizzy drinks. A fairly standard Italian buffet was $240 (for the four of us with drinks and service on top). Yes, its stunning, the rooms are eco friendly, but for a family with teenagers who like to do activities…

data.text: Our stay at the Wild Orchid was both comfortable and relaxing. Located in the city center, we were steps away from downtown restaurants and shops. The room itself had a queen sized bed with a balcony, with a private bathroom and a wonderful air conditioner (We needed it!), and free wifi. The bed was comfortable, the space was larger, and the balcony was a welcome site. We would absolutely recommend the Wild Orchid while staying in Hue.

European breakfast was the same standard as every other 3 star hotel in Vietnam...pretty standard but not an issue! In our opinion, it’s not easy to walk to the ancient town from the hotel (approx 30 mins and quite boring!). If you’re happy to cycle it takes less that 10 mins on the free bikes supplied by the hotel. I found this tricky as I’m not confident on a bicycle so this is just something to note. By taxi it costs around 40,000vnd. Otherwise excellent stay and would recommend!

We glad we went out and explored because that also made our holiday.

It is reasonably well placed, about the right price, though please keep a check on your passports and valuables in this insecure setting.

data.text: My boyfriend and I arrived in Vietnam last week and our first stop in the country was Nova hotel. We received such a warm welcome from all the staff as well as some great information about the city and surrounding area for the entirety of our stay there. Breakfast everyday was perfect (we even got a wake up call one morning when they suspected we were going to sleep in for breakfast!) and evening food there also good on the occasion we went for it. The room itself is so comfortable, bed was great which can be a rarity in Asia. The bathroom also came with small toiletries which was handy. I couldn't recommend this hotel enough, they have thought of everything. A really relaxing base for the start of your time in Vietnam, excellent :)

data.text: My wife and I stayed here for three nights. The hotel itself is very nice, clean, and in a good location, quiet area, close to the touristy spots. The owner, Dzung, went above and beyond to make our visit a great one; his whole family is so friendly. The home-cooked breakfast in the morning is delicious (our favorite was the pancakes with banana), Dzung's wife cooks up some great tasting dinners as well! There are bicycles available to borrow, but taxi services are also available if you want to get further out from the town. Overall, we'd highly recommend this hotel, and wouldn't hesitate to stay again.

The pool is quite small, however this is not a large hotel so as there are not many guests it does not feel crowded. Although we were only here for 1 night and 2 days we used the pool 3 times and on 2 occasions we were the only people in it. The breakfast was delicious and unlimited. You could also borrow bikes for free from the hotel to travel into the city centre. It is excellent value for money for the service and quality of the hotel.

data.text: My wife and I had a rewarding, but rainy experience staying at the Ana Mandara Villas. The location was private, scenic and quiet, which seems like it was far away from the hustle of downtown Da Lat. The food and wait service in the restaurant was a delightful surprise that we enjoyed coming back for more. We also used the services of the local spa and their complimentary steam/sauna rooms. The villa was extremely spacious and aesthetically pleasing, but a little musty smelling (might have been climate-related). Moderately priced accommodations for us during our trip to Vietnam (compared to what we pay for similar accommodations in US). We look forward to visiting again.

Staff were incredible efficient and friendly at check-in despite the language barriers. However, from the moment I walked into this place until we got into our room I knew I would not stay there voluntarily. The lobby like so much else in this place was not maintained at all. There were two very sad-looking fountains (no plants whatsoever, just a basin with water, really) and lots of stacked card board boxes. All of this made for a very unprofessional appeal. Once we were in the room (which was very clean, but the furniture was well past it's prime) we immediately noticed the moldy smell. Though we didn't see any mold the smell was so pungent that we left the room…
